headline: Red day — HRV and sleep debt say protect today, and the plan already has you down for an easy 7K, not a harder session.
body_state: Readiness 33.6 — low band, driver is sleep. HRV last night 36 ms sits below your normal range (deterministic verdict: postpone quality, easy running only today). 14-day sleep debt has built to 25 h; overnight body-battery recharge was a modest +45. This follows a real bounce: readiness climbed 52 (8/11) → 48 (8/12) → 49 (8/13) after bottoming at 11 on 8/10, then dropped back to 36 overnight. Garmin status reads Recovery. TSB is -17, still inside the -5…-30 productive-training band — fitness isn't the problem, recovery is.
session: Today's 7 km easy run @ 4:50-5:19/km is already the right call — no quality scheduled. Keep it conversational, RPE 3-4; if HR creeps past ~75% max, slow down regardless of pace. Cadence has been sitting 154-163 spm on recent runs, below your 168-172 target — count 30 right-foot strikes per 20s and nudge it up with shorter steps, not longer ones. Nothing booked on the calendar today.
recent: Yesterday's Un1t (41 min, avg HR 133) was a sustainable zone-2/3 stimulus but ran 3.8 min short of its 45-min booking. Aug 12's tempo run undershot harder: only 2.98 of 4 km at threshold, pace 4:38/km (6-20 s/km slow), HR topped 156 — 7 bpm under your 163 LT — despite an RPE-8 rating. That hard-feeling-but-not-actually-hard mismatch, plus a weak 13 bpm HR recovery that day, is the same under-recovery signal today's readiness verdict is flagging. Intensity distribution is still skewed (21.9% easy vs the 80% target), so grey-zone training is the throughline this week, not one bad day.
focus: Easy 7K only today — no quality, cap effort at RPE 3-4 / ~75% max HR.
Sleep debt is 25h over 14 days — earlier bedtime this week to pay it down.
Slow the easy days down: 21.9% easy vs 80% target is why hard sessions have been feeling harder than the numbers say.
